chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Functional decline affects more than one-third of adults over 65, driving ~3 million emergency visits and $50 billion yearly. Frailty tools need manual assessments and capture only a single timepoint. A hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL stable for three years means different risk than one that fell from 13.5 g/dL. No large-scale study has tested whether routine lab trajectories alone predict pre-clinical decline.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem as predicting pre-clinical functional mobility decline in older adults using longitudinal trajectories of routine biomarkers before observable impairment or falls occur.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: Each biomarker gave five descriptors - mean, SD, delta, count and slope - yielding 80 trajectory features plus age and gender. Four classifiers (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) were trained with 5-fold cross-validation and out-of-fold evaluation.
chk_method.reason: The poster correctly describes the feature engineering of longitudinal trajectory descriptors and the use of LightGBM and other machine learning algorithms.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: Cases came from ICD-10 mobility codes in All of Us (OMOP, Controlled Tier v8); controls received a random pseudo-index date, preventing immortal time bias. Twelve biomarkers were drawn from a three-year pre-index window.
chk_data.reason: The poster accurately identifies the dataset as 297,861 participants from the All of Us Research Program Controlled Tier Dataset version 8, including 33,088 cases of mobility decline.
